target.title: Settings: add unified usage and spend dashboard
target.body:
## Product case

CodexBar has detailed provider views but no single Settings destination that answers three basic questions together: what did I spend, which subscriptions drove it, and which models did I use most? This PR adds a local, spend-first dashboard using CodexBar's existing history rather than a new analytics service.

The intentionally narrow v1 is **local exploration**:

- no upload, telemetry, hosted account, or new persistence format;
- no prompts, projects, paths, emails, or account identities in the dashboard model;
- unknown or unpriced history remains visibly unavailable rather than becoming `$0`;
- 7- and 30-day windows are computed from the same local daily entries.

## What this adds

- A persisted **Usage & Spend** destination in the existing Settings sidebar.
- 7/30-day estimated spend, tracked-token, and priced-history coverage summaries.
- Ranked subscription rows, including distinct identity-free Codex account rows.
- Cross-subscription model rankings and a daily estimated-spend chart.
- Existing CodexBar panels, provider colors/icons, native controls, localization, dark mode, empty states, and reduced-motion behavior.

## Account-complete data contract

`ProviderInput` is subscription-scoped rather than provider-unique. Multiple Codex accounts remain separate rows and all contribute to totals, daily points, and model aggregates.

The active Codex account reuses the normal provider cost snapshot. Each sibling account scans its own Codex home into a separate hashed cache, with Pi session history disabled for sibling scans so shared Pi history is counted exactly once. Failed or unavailable history remains a visible unpriced subscription row.

No account identity, path, project, prompt, or credential crosses into the dashboard presentation model.

## Real configured runtime proof

These are identity-free captures from a signed native app built from this branch at `75e29b59`. They use the machine's existing configured provider histories; no account identity, email, path, prompt, project, token, or credential appears. The proof-only docs commit is `d37080a8`.

The complete capture notes and evidence boundary are in [`docs/usage-spend-dashboard-runtime-proof.md`](https://github.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/blob/codex/unified-spend-dashboard/docs/usage-spend-dashboard-runtime-proof.md).

### Configured 30-day data

![Configured 30-day Usage and Spend dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/unified-spend-dashboard/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-real-30d.png)

### Configured 7-day data

![Configured 7-day Usage and Spend dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/unified-spend-dashboard/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-real-7d.png)

### Refresh in progress

The action disables and becomes a native progress indicator while provider and Codex-account histories reload.

![Usage and Spend refresh in progress](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/unified-spend-dashboard/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-real-refreshing.png)

### Refresh completed

The selected 7-day window remains in place, the progress indicator clears, and newly scanned Codex history updates the aggregate and row values without a stale overwrite.

![Usage and Spend after refresh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/codex/unified-spend-dashboard/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-real-after-refresh.png)

Closing and reopening Settings returned to this pane, and `defaults read com.steipete.codexbar settingsSelectedPane` returned `usageSpend`.

This machine has one Codex account, so the runtime proof does not pretend to show a live Codex account switch. The focused suite covers two distinct Codex subscription snapshots, active-account reload identity changes, stale-snapshot rejection, and cancellation-safe replacement.

## Additional sanitized fixture coverage

These simulated fixtures cover distinct Codex accounts, dark appearance, and the empty/unpriced state without exposing private data.

### Light - 30 days - multiple Codex accounts

![Usage and Spend light 30-day dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/b425f6bac051f2bee8e4145b6ff97a1d4138961a/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-light-30d.png)

### Dark - 7 days - multiple Codex accounts

![Usage and Spend dark 7-day dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/b425f6bac051f2bee8e4145b6ff97a1d4138961a/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-dark-7d.png)

### Empty/unpriced history

![Usage and Spend empty dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chipagosfinest/CodexBar/b425f6bac051f2bee8e4145b6ff97a1d4138961a/docs/screenshots/usage-spend-dashboard-empty.png)

## Relationship to sharing

- Companion PR: [#2112 - Add local shareable usage card](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2112)
- This PR owns persistent in-app exploration only.
- #2112 owns export/share actions only.
- Neither branch depends on the other at build or runtime.

## Why a dedicated pane

The top-level destination remains a product decision, not an implementation inevitability. A dedicated pane avoids overloading provider settings or the menu, provides enough width for aligned comparisons, and keeps trend analysis out of the fast-glance path. If maintainers prefer an existing shared overview, the aggregation model can survive while presentation moves.

## Verification

- [x] `swift build`
- [x] `swift test --filter UnifiedSpendDashboardModelTests` - 5 focused tests passed
- [x] `make check`
- [x] Production target compiles after the account-complete repair
- [x] Real configured runtime proof: 7/30-day windows, refresh in progress/completed, cache update, and persisted pane
- [x] Sanitized fixture proof: distinct Codex accounts, dark appearance, and empty/unpriced history
- [ ] Full sharded suite on the current proof commit

The local bundled-app widget step is blocked by an installed Xcode `IDESimulatorFoundation` / `DVTDownloads` plug-in mismatch. This is machine-local; the CodexBar app target builds cleanly, and the PR's fresh GitHub CI is the authoritative bundle/test result.

## Product/design decision requested

`VISION.md` requires sign-off for new product surfaces. The implementation, account-completeness blocker, and inspectable real runtime proof are now addressed. This PR asks whether CodexBar should keep a permanent top-level spend-first dashboard or present the same aggregation inside an existing shared overview.

target.title: fix: Linux SIGILL during timezone resolution on non-FHS systems (fixes #2127)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2127 

- Bootstrap timezone discovery before the Linux CLI enters Commander/Foundation-dependent setup.
- When `TZ` is unset and `/etc/localtime` is readable, direct Swift Foundation to the system timezone file.
- Preserve all explicitly configured `TZ` values.
- Add focused Linux regression coverage for fallback and no-op behavior.

## Problem

On NixOS, running a provider usage command with `TZ` unset terminates the process with `SIGILL` (#2127):

```console
$ codexbar usage --provider claude
fish: Job 1, "codexbar usage --provider claude" terminated by signal SIGILL (Illegal instruction)
```

This reproduced with:

- both v0.42.1 Linux x86_64 release artifacts (glibc and musl);
- an unmodified build of `main` at `c852c135`;
- NixOS 26.05 with `/etc/localtime` pointing into the Nix store; and
- no conventional `/usr/share/zoneinfo` directory.

Debugger inspection reaches Swift Foundation timezone conversion around `TimeZone._cfObject`, where execution ends at an intentional `ud2` trap.

## Root cause

Swift Foundation attempts to resolve the process default timezone through conventional Linux zoneinfo locations. NixOS uses a non-FHS layout: the valid system timezone is available through `/etc/localtime`, which points to timezone data in the Nix store.

When `TZ` is absent, Foundation does not discover that valid configuration and traps while constructing the default timezone.

## Fix

`CodexBarCLI.main()` now performs a small Linux-only timezone bootstrap before argument parsing, Commander descriptor construction, logging, or provider work.

The bootstrap:

- runs only on Linux;
- leaves `TZ` untouched whenever the variable is already present;
- verifies that `/etc/localtime` is readable before using it;
- uses the absolute timezone-file form expected by the supported Linux runtimes; and
- becomes a no-op when no usable fallback is available.

The environment change is process-local. It does not modify system configuration or the environment of the calling shell.

## Regression coverage

`CLITimeZoneBootstrapTests` covers:

- selecting `/etc/localtime` when `TZ` is absent and the file is readable;
- preserving named, empty, and custom-path `TZ` values; and
- declining to set a fallback when `/etc/localtime` is unreadable.

The policy logic is tested as a pure helper so the suite does not mutate process-global environment state or become order-dependent under parallel execution.

## Scope and compatibility

- No provider fetching, authentication, account storage, or parsing behavior changes.
- No dependency, package, toolchain, or release-process changes.
- No macOS behavior changes.
- Conventional Linux distributions continue using their configured system timezone.
- Systems without a readable `/etc/localtime` retain the existing behavior.
- Explicit caller timezone configuration always takes precedence.

## Validation

- [x] `swift test --filter CLITimeZoneBootstrapTests` — 3 tests passed
- [x] `make test` — all 31 Linux test selections passed in 3 groups with no retries or failures
- [x] `./Scripts/lint.sh lint-linux` — portable checks passed; SwiftLint reported 0 violations across 1,425 files
- [x] SwiftFormat 0.61.1 on both changed Swift files — `0/2 files require formatting`
- [x] `swift build -c release --product CodexBarCLI --static-swift-stdlib`
- [x] `--help` and `--version` smoke tests with `TZ` unset
- [x] Affected `usage --provider claude` command on NixOS with `TZ` unset — exited normally and returned usage instead of `SIGILL`
- [x] `make check` passed all relevant checks for the changed files; the full Linux CI lint path also passes.

No UI changes; screenshots are not applicable.

target.title: fix(sweep): bound failed shard recovery
target.body:
## Summary

Makes failed review-shard recovery durable, one-shot, and non-actionable. A recovery now waits for an acknowledged exact-review queue write instead of treating a GitHub event delivery as proof that a replacement review run exists.

## Problem

The failed-shard recovery job could send a `repository_dispatch` event and accept GitHub's HTTP acknowledgement as success. The later legacy router could then create repeated replacement `workflow_dispatch` runs for stale open items after the originating worker had finished. That bypassed the durable queue/lease decision at the point where failure was detected.

This was not author activity. For example, a scheduled sweep selected a large ClawHub set and its recovery fanned out directly:

- Parent scheduled run: [Review ClawSweeper items #29261805316](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29261805316), created 2026-07-13 15:20:23 UTC; it selected 30 ClawHub shards and failed.
- Recovery run: [Review event items #29263452346](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29263452346), created 2026-07-13 15:43:49 UTC and completed 15:56:22 UTC; it directly fanned out 29 ClawHub items, including `#2411`, `#2460`, `#2487`, `#2489`, `#2490`, `#2873`, `#2898`, `#2947`, `#2948`, `#2949`, `#2950`, `#2951`, `#2953`, `#2957`, `#2958`, `#2959`, `#2963`, `#2964`, `#2969`, `#2986`, `#3005`, `#3006`, `#3023`, `#3036`, `#3037`, `#3038`, `#3050`, `#3055`, and `#3056`.
- Earlier examples show the same pre-fix pattern: [#29249741130](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29249741130) (34-item batch), [#29253817069](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29253817069) (34-item batch), and [#29257701833](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29257701833) (36-item batch).

The same mechanism explains the observed stale OpenClaw direct-review churn, including [openclaw/openclaw#67967](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67967), [#92328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/92328), and [#84975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84975). These are recovery fan-outs, not fresh review requests.

Separately, a live exact-review action-ledger publish on this PR's review run failed after eight non-fast-forward retries: [run #29262649242](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29262649242) / [job #86859694467](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29262649242/job/86859694467). That shared-state write contention is a distinct control-plane issue and is being investigated separately; this PR does not claim to solve it.

## Implementation

- Replace the failed-shard `repository_dispatch` hop with a signed POST directly to the existing durable `/internal/exact-review/enqueue` endpoint.
- Require a positive queue acknowledgement: queued, deduplicated, or explicitly disabled. A missing or invalid acknowledgement remains a failed recovery and is retried at most three times; it cannot be silently treated as delivered.
- Reduce the recovery job permissions to `actions: read` and `contents: read`.
- Preserve the target branch, make recovery review-only, and suppress direct and deferred verdict routing so recovery cannot close the target item.
- Publish the review-only recovery's durable comment without `clawsweeper-verdict` or `clawsweeper-action` markers. This preserves the review record/version marker but prevents the scheduled comment router from later interpreting a recovery result as a close, repair, or merge instruction.
- Enforce the queue invariant: a failed-shard recovery may create one item, but can never supersede pending, dispatching, or leased ordinary work or an active recovery. Expired leases are reclaimed before this decision, allowing a new recovery only when no live work remains.
- Add queue and workflow assertions for direct durable enqueue, acknowledgement handling, disabled-target handling, active/expired lease behavior, and non-actionable review-only publication.

## Separate operational tracks

- [PR #539](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/539) tracks restoration of the `openclaw-clawsweeper` GitHub App installation permissions for `openclaw/openclaw` (**Issues: Read and write** and **Pull requests: Read and write**). Permission 403s for comments, labels, or closes must not be used to judge this queue-recovery canary.
- CSW-034 tracks `clawsweeper-state` concurrent-write / non-fast-forward serialization. State publication contention must likewise be reported separately from whether this recovery enqueues once and avoids direct fan-out.

## Validation

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/clawsweeper.ts src/repair/publish-event-result.ts test/clawsweeper.test.ts test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run build` — passed.
- `node --test test/clawsweeper.test.ts` — 75 passed.
- `node --test --test-name-pattern="failed review recovery waits" test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — 1 passed.
- Linux proof: local-container Crabbox lease `cbx_764df5e94382` (`node:24-bookworm`) ran `corepack pnpm run build && node --test test/clawsweeper.test.ts && node --test --test-name-pattern 'failed review recovery waits' test/sweep-workflow.test.ts` — exit 0; 75 + 1 tests passed.
- Supplemental Linux queue/lease proof: local-container Crabbox lease `cbx_4d4775cfb925` (`node:24-bookworm`) ran `corepack pnpm run build` plus six focused tests — four real `ExactReviewQueue` handler cases for recovery completion and preserved pending/leased ownership, one marker-suppression case, and the durable-ack/no-fan-out/bounded-attempt workflow assertion. All passed; exit 0.

The full workflow-helper suite has native-Windows baseline failures because this host's `docker-desktop` WSL distribution has no `/bin/bash`; that is a Linux-hosted helper surface, not a product-platform regression. The changed workflow assertion was validated in the Linux container above.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` — clean; no actionable findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main` — clean against current main; no actionable regressions.

## Maintainer proof decision and monitored canary

Current status: implementation and automated proof are ready; no after-fix production failed-shard event exists yet. Creating one artificially would create control-plane load and require prohibited manual workflow dispatch, rerun, cancellation, or an induced worker failure. The supplemental local-container proof above exercises the real queue handler and workflow sources deterministically, but not a deployed queue, a GitHub Actions job, or live runner step state; it cannot substitute for the requested staging/production observation.

Maintainer decision required before taking this PR out of draft:

1. **Approve a monitored canary proof override**, or
2. **Hold for staging/shadow or naturally occurring post-deploy proof**.

If option 1 is approved, the first naturally occurring failed shard is the only canary trigger. Do not manually dispatch, rerun, cancel, or manufacture a failure. Capture a redacted linked run/log showing all of these invariants:

- exactly one signed queue acknowledgement (`queued`, `deduped`, or explicitly `accepted=false`);
- no recovery-created `workflow_dispatch` run titled `Review event items …` and no recovery fan-out;
- recovery does not supersede ordinary pending, dispatching, or leased work, nor a live recovery;
- direct and deferred verdict-router steps are skipped;
- the durable recovery comment has neither `clawsweeper-verdict:` nor `clawsweeper-action:` markers, so the scheduled router cannot close, repair, or merge from it;
- recovery completes terminally if it fails, with no retry loop beyond its bounded enqueue attempts.

Immediate rollback criterion: if any invariant fails, revert the #518 merge commit immediately and preserve the redacted run/queue evidence for follow-up. Do not use App-permission changes or state-branch retry changes as a rollback substitute for this code path.

## Rollout and risk

This changes failed-shard recovery scheduling and publication only; fresh review requests retain normal queue/retry behavior. The workflow uses the existing `CLAWSWEEPER_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and touching `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` carries the normal GitHub OAuth/workflow scope risk. The PR remains a draft solely pending the maintainer proof/canary decision above.

target.title: Add ZenMux Management API provider
target.body:
## Summary

Adds ZenMux as a disabled-by-default API provider using the documented read-only Management API.

- Reads the rolling five-hour and seven-day quota windows from `GET /api/v1/management/subscription/detail`.
- Shows subscription tier, renewal date, non-healthy account status, reset countdowns, and compact used/max flow details.
- Enriches the snapshot with PAYG balance from `GET /api/v1/management/payg/balance`; a non-auth balance failure does not discard valid quota data.
- Renders PAYG balance as a compact credits row instead of exposing provider setup copy in the menu card.
- Accepts a ZenMux Management API key from provider config or `ZENMUX_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY`. Standard inference API keys are rejected with an actionable error.
- Wires provider registration, settings, CLI diagnostics, icon/widget exhaustiveness, cost-scan exclusion, docs, provider counts, and the generated social card.

## Security and privacy

- Requests are limited to the fixed `https://zenmux.ai/api/v1/management` origin and use the shared redirect-guarded transport.
- No endpoint override, browser cookie, dashboard session, inference prompt, or request log is read.
- Requests are timeout-bounded; cancellation is preserved, including during optional balance enrichment.
- ZenMux identity is provider-siloed and contains plan/status only; no identity is borrowed from another provider.

Official API references:

- https://docs.zenmux.ai/api/platform/subscription-detail
- https://docs.zenmux.ai/api/platform/payg-balance

## Validation

- `swift test --filter ZenMuxProviderTests`: 10/10 passed, including the final menu-card labels and layout model.
- `make check`: passed; SwiftFormat clean, SwiftLint 0 violations, generated parser hash/docs/locales/package gates current.
- `./Scripts/package_app.sh`: passed.
- Packaged `CodexBar.app` embeds exact commit `3a053d9f`; `codesign --verify --deep --strict CodexBar.app` passed.
- The exact-head packaged CLI completed an authenticated production Management API fetch. Redacted shape: both quota windows had numeric utilization/flow details and ISO-8601 reset timestamps; the subscription had an ISO-8601 renewal timestamp; PAYG returned a positive numeric credit balance. No key, account identifier, exact balance, or exact usage value is included here.

`make test` is not recorded as green: it discovered 639 selections in 54 groups, then stopped in group 3 after the untouched `AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` race failed both the first pass and full-group retry. An isolated suite rerun reproduced the same existing timing behavior (`completedRefreshCountForTesting` became 2 instead of 1). No adaptive-refresh source or tests are changed by this PR.

## Redacted exact-head runtime proof

Validated July 13, 2026 using the packaged app from exact branch head `3a053d9f314d9cff443713bd8d4338f10178b5fe`:

```console
$ git rev-parse HEAD
3a053d9f314d9cff443713bd8d4338f10178b5fe

$ /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy -c "Print :CodexGitCommit" CodexBar.app/Contents/Info.plist
3a053d9f

$ codesign --verify --deep --strict CodexBar.app
# exit 0
```

The bundled CLI then completed a live authenticated Management API refresh. The following privacy projection was produced directly from that CLI JSON. It retains window lengths, field types, and presence checks while suppressing the API key, subscription tier, exact flow counts, utilization values, reset/renewal timestamps, and credit balance.

```json
{
  "provider": "zenmux",
  "source": "api",
  "usage": {
    "primary": {
      "windowMinutes": 300,
      "usedPercentType": "number",
      "resetTimestampPresent": true,
      "flowDetailPresent": true
    },
    "secondary": {
      "windowMinutes": 10080,
      "usedPercentType": "number",
      "resetTimestampPresent": true,
      "flowDetailPresent": true
    },
    "subscriptionTierPresent": true,
    "subscriptionRenewalTimestampPresent": true
  },
  "credits": {
    "remainingType": "number",
    "positiveBalancePresent": true
  }
}
```

This demonstrates that the live exact-head response populates the five-hour and weekly meters, both reset fields, compact flow details, subscription tier and renewal metadata, and the numeric PAYG balance consumed by the compact Credits row. Healthy account status is intentionally omitted by the UI; non-healthy statuses remain covered by focused presentation tests.

## Authenticated evidence

Exact-head live verification used a separately configured ZenMux Management API key. The key remained local and was never printed, committed, or passed to the PR. The packaged CLI confirmed both documented routes, quota reset timestamps, renewal mapping, flow details, and PAYG balance. The output above is intentionally shape-only to avoid publishing account telemetry.

target.title: Scope quota warning state to accounts
target.body:
## Summary

- key static quota-warning episodes by a stable account discriminator instead of provider/window alone
- forward account ownership through ordinary refresh, selected token-account, stacked Codex, and Claude OAuth/CLI publication paths
- reconcile Claude extra-window warning state per account while preserving provider-wide cleanup when a warning window is disabled
- add focused regressions for ordinary refresh, selected outcomes, stacked Codex accounts, Claude sibling accounts, and provider-wide cleanup

## Root cause

`QuotaWarningStateKey` previously contained only the provider, warning window, and optional extra-window ID. When users switched accounts, one account's observation could clear, suppress, or re-arm another account's threshold episode. The stacked selected-Codex publication path also did not run the static threshold reducer.

This change separates the opaque state discriminator from the optional display identity. Stable token-account UUIDs and hashed provider ownership keys scope reducer state; notification copy still follows the existing Hide Personal Info setting.

## Runtime proof

I ran an identical disposable harness at base `c852c135` and current head `be7f11c4`. It drives the production `UsageStore.refreshProvider` path through six ordinary selected-account refreshes, with two synthetic token accounts and fixture-only provider outcomes. A notifier spy records the same `QuotaWarningEvent` passed to the notification layer.

Sequence: A 40%, B 40%, A 55%, B 30%, A 55%, B 55%, with a 50%-remaining threshold.

Base shared-state trace:

```text
step=3 account=Account-A used=55
emitted account=Account-A threshold=50 remaining=45
step=5 account=Account-A used=55
emitted account=Account-A threshold=50 remaining=45
step=6 account=Account-B used=55
summary emitted=Account-A,Account-A
```

Account B's recovery re-armed A, so A emitted twice; B's own crossing was then suppressed.

Current-head account-scoped trace:

```text
step=3 account=Account-A used=55
emitted account=Account-A threshold=50 remaining=45
step=5 account=Account-A used=55
step=6 account=Account-B used=55
emitted account=Account-B threshold=50 remaining=45
summary emitted=Account-A,Account-B
```

Each account retained an independent episode: no duplicate A warning and no suppressed B warning. Both runs passed one test in one suite using:

```sh
CODEXBAR_SUPPRESS_TEST_KEYCHAIN_ACCESS=1 swift test --filter QuotaWarningAccountRuntimeProofTests
```

The proof used isolated settings, synthetic labels/tokens, and stubbed provider outcomes. It did not read a real account store, browser data, provider session, or Keychain item; the disposable harness was not added to either branch.

## Validation

- `CODEXBAR_SUPPRESS_TEST_KEYCHAIN_ACCESS=1 OS_ACTIVITY_MODE=disable swift test --filter 'UsageStoreAccountQuotaWarningTests|UsageStoreSessionQuotaTransitionTests|CodexSessionQuotaFalseRestoreTests|ClaudeExtraWindowQuotaWarningTests|PredictivePaceWarningTests'` - 86 tests in 5 suites passed
- `make check` - passed; SwiftFormat reported 0 files requiring formatting and SwiftLint reported 0 violations across 1,426 files
- `make test` on this commit combined with the test-only isolation from #2128 - all 639 selections passed across 54/54 groups, with zero first-pass failures, retries, or timeouts
- disposable merge simulation against current #2001 head `b14629bd` - 51 focused tests in 5 suites passed; `make check` reported 0/1,437 files requiring formatting and 0 SwiftLint violations across 1,436 files; `git diff --check` passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

## Coordination with #2001

#2001 now has a dedicated `QuotaLowHookUsageKey` at head `b14629bd`, but derives its account key from `snapshot.accountEmail`. That compiles independently, yet is not a sufficient stable discriminator: Claude OAuth accounts can be email-less, generic token accounts can fall back to mutable or duplicate labels, and Codex owners can share an email across workspace/source/auth contexts.

The refreshed disposable merge simulation produced exactly one conflicted file, `UsageStore+QuotaWarnings.swift`, with two adjacent regions. The minimal correct union is to keep #2001's dedicated hook key, notification-independent hook dispatch, and payload behavior while feeding this PR's `accountContext.discriminator` into `dispatchQuotaLowHooks(accountKey:)`; `accountContext.displayName` remains presentation-only.

The combined tree passed 51 focused warning/hook tests across five suites, including a simulation-only regression proving two email-less Claude owners keep separate hook baselines while native notifications are disabled. It also passed `make check` and `git diff --check`. No published branch was changed.

Whichever PR lands second must carry that union and the email-less hook regression. If #2001 lands first, this PR will be rebased and the integration included before merge.

A recording was not available because the host was locked; the exact-head packaged-app runtime log is included above.

## Fresh-bundle runtime proof

I also ran the freshly packaged current-head app, not the disposable harness:

```text
head=be7f11c4ffdc5249a7409af5cd7c50b17eb66869
bundle_embedded_commit=be7f11c4
bundle_binary_sha256=6b4392eef2d9574a1b8929eceea8f12b97ae3f8a7bbaaa4bc582d8db9007b8a6
build=CODEXBAR_ALLOW_LLDB=1 ./Scripts/package_app.sh debug
```

The exact unmodified bundle ran with an isolated HOME/CODEX_HOME/config, both Keychain-access guards set, and only sub2api enabled against a loopback HTTP fixture. The two token accounts had synthetic labels and fixed UUIDs. This does not claim authenticated-provider behavior and did not read a real provider account, browser store, or Keychain item.

Because the host was locked, I drove the same production operations used by the segmented account switcher under LLDB: `setActiveTokenAccountIndex`, cached-account activation, and `refreshProvider(.sub2api)`. Provider outcomes were not stubbed: the packaged app used its production Sub2API URLSession fetcher against the loopback server, then its production reducer, `SessionQuotaNotifier`, and `QuotaWarningAlertOverlayController`.

The redacted server trace was:

```text
[FETCH 01] account=A used=40    # A baseline
[FETCH 02] account=B used=40    # B baseline
[CONTROL] account=A used=55
[FETCH 03] account=A used=55    # A crosses
[FETCH 04] account=B used=40    # B unchanged; no false alert
[FETCH 05] account=A used=55    # repeated low A; no duplicate
[CONTROL] account=B used=55
[FETCH 06] account=B used=55    # B crosses
[FETCH 07] account=B used=55    # repeated low B; no duplicate
```

The real notifier breakpoint was hit exactly twice:

```text
[NOTIFIER 1] account=Proof Account A provider=sub2api window=session threshold=50 remaining=45
2026-07-14 04:53:54.265 [sessionQuotaNotifications] enqueuing (prefix=quota-warning-sub2api-session-50)
2026-07-14 04:53:54.277 [sessionQuotaNotifications] Presenting quota warning overlay

[NOTIFIER 2] account=Proof Account B provider=sub2api window=session threshold=50 remaining=45
2026-07-14 04:56:29.991 [sessionQuotaNotifications] enqueuing (prefix=quota-warning-sub2api-session-50)
2026-07-14 04:56:29.997 [sessionQuotaNotifications] Presenting quota warning overlay

breakpoint hit count = 2
```

The debug bundle was not authorized for Notification Center, so its native UNUserNotificationCenter posts were skipped; the enabled on-screen alert path did present twice. The final in-process state contained exactly two independent owner keys:

```text
owner=token-account:11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111 window=session fired=50 remaining=45
owner=token-account:22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222 window=session fired=50 remaining=45
cached snapshots: Proof Account A=55%, Proof Account B=55%
```

The source worktree remained clean. The temporary server/app were stopped, the pre-run debug preference snapshot was restored exactly, and the installed release app was left running.

target.title: fix(local-review): use selected Codex CLI
target.body:
## Summary

Use the operator-selected Codex CLI for local-only reviews and matching local preflight, while preserving a Windows Desktop Codex fallback when no runnable PATH launcher exists.

## Problem

`review --local-only` injected `CLAWSWEEPER_PREFER_WINDOWS_CODEX_APP=1`, forcing the Windows Desktop app binary at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\codex.exe`. On the reported host that binary is stale and rejects the requested model, while the user's normal `PATH` Codex CLI works. The local preflight selected the same Desktop binary, which could validate a different executable than the review runner.

## Implementation

- Stop forcing the Desktop app binary for local-only reviews and local preflight.
- Preserve explicit `CODEX_BIN` precedence.
- On Windows, resolve in order: explicit `CODEX_BIN`, the first spawnable PATH `codex`, then the installed Desktop binary only if PATH has no runnable launcher.
- Prefer a real `PATHEXT` launcher over npm's co-located extensionless shell shim; skip unsupported shims and continue searching later PATH entries.
- Resolve relative PATH entries from the worker's actual launch directory so preflight and the review subprocess make the same selection.
- Document the ordered behavior and add focused regression coverage.

Production `.github/actions/setup-codex` remains separate and pinned at `@openai/codex` `0.139.0`; this PR does not modify it.

## Validation

- `node --test test/codex-process.test.ts test/command.test.ts test/clawsweeper.test.ts` — passed (90 tests).
- `pnpm run build:all` — passed.
- `pnpm run lint:scripts` — passed for the original local-preflight script change; the follow-up changes no scripts.
- Focused `oxfmt --check` for all changed source, documentation, and test files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Native Windows preflight: `pnpm run codex:local:check` — passed. It selected `C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe ... C:\Users\marti\AppData\Roaming\npm\codex.cmd` and completed the `gpt-5.6-sol` smoke test.
- Native Windows local runner: `pnpm run review -- --local-only --target-repo openclaw/clawsweeper --target-dir <clean detached checkout> --item-number 541 --artifact-dir <temp>` — completed successfully in 3m54s with local-only artifacts only; no GitHub comment, label, or branch mutation was performed.
- `pnpm run check` previously completed build and lint, then hit unrelated native-Windows prerequisite failures in existing unit tests: unavailable WSL `/bin/bash` for Bash-helper tests, Windows symlink permissions, and `npm.cmd` `EINVAL` in runtime packaging. This PR does not broaden into test-harness or platform-policy changes.

Proof boundary: native Windows local launcher selection only; no workflow or CI-matrix changes.

## Codex review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted` initially identified three accepted P2 edge cases: an unspawnable extensionless shim, relative PATH entries resolved from the wrong cwd, and a valid later PATH launcher shadowed by an unsupported earlier shim. Each was fixed with regression coverage.
- Final `codex review --uncommitted`: clean — no blocking correctness issues.
- `codex review --base origin/main` after commit `a6163ddff2`: clean — explicit overrides, runnable PATH selection, and Desktop fallback were all verified.

## Risks and rollout

Windows local-only review now preserves desktop-only installations while preventing a stale Desktop binary from overriding the user's working PATH CLI. The behavior is limited to local launcher selection and uses no local CLI pin or update. Production setup remains unchanged. This branch is independent of #539.
